=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2994 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2]
  PROBLEM: `gh issue list --limit 200` can omit an existing open fix-up issue from the dedupe search once the open `ai:orchestrator-managed` set exceeds 200 items.
  WHY: If the matching issue is beyond the first 200 results, the query will not see it and the workflow can create a duplicate fix-up.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2999-3000 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3_1-pro-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: jq `contains()` on the Local ID and tracking issue fields can substring-match a different open issue when IDs share a prefix, so deduplication may reuse the wrong fix-up issue.
  WHY: Deepseek also noted the Local ID collision (`validation-fix-cycle-2` vs `validation-fix-cycle-20`), and the other four reviewers independently confirmed the tracking-issue collision (`#1043` vs `#10430`).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2994 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `gh issue list --limit 200` can omit an existing open fix-up issue from the dedupe search once the open `ai:orchestrator-managed` set exceeds 200 items.
  WHY: If the matching issue is beyond the first 200 results, the query will not see it and the workflow can create a duplicate fix-up.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:3000 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: jq `contains()` on the Local ID and tracking issue fields can substring-match the wrong open issue when IDs share a prefix.
  WHY: `contains("Local ID: \`validation-fix-cycle-2\`")` can match `validation-fix-cycle-20`, and `contains("Tracking issue: #1043")` can match `#10430`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-pro-preview ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:3000 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `contains($trk)` performs substring matching, so `Tracking issue: #1043` can falsely match `Tracking issue: #10430`.
  WHY: That can cause the orchestrator to reuse the wrong issue and skip creating the distinct fix-up for the current tracker.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-pro-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:3000 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `contains($trk)` performs substring matching, so deduplication can reuse the wrong fix-up issue when tracking numbers share a prefix.
  WHY: For example, a body containing `Tracking issue: #10430` matches a search for `Tracking issue: #1043`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:3000 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `contains($trk)` performs substring matching, so a lookup for `Tracking issue: #1043` can match an issue body for `Tracking issue: #10430`.
  WHY: That can make the workflow reuse the wrong open fix-up and skip creating the correct one.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2999 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The jq `contains()` check for tracking issue numbers can false-positive on prefix collisions, causing the wrong open fix-up issue to be reused.
  WHY: It can match `Tracking issue: #1043` against `Tracking issue: #10430`, which misattributes the validation failure.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
